$comment: The Contributing Member explainer (/contributing/; /pin/ redirects here). Unlisted, like /roles/: linked only from /roles/ and kept out of search engines until the board approves the ranks. The pin on its own is the Contributing Member pin; Reviewer, Committer and Maintainer each add a ring. Brass for regional work, silver for national. Summarises design/research/recognition-system.md. [PLACEHOLDER] marks what's still open.
title: Contributing Member
description: The Contributing Member pin, and the three rings that can grow around it. What each one says about the person wearing it. A working draft.
draft: A working draft. The board hasn't approved the ranks yet, and the pin is still being made. Everything here is what we're building toward.

title: Contributing
Member
hero.lede: For the people who leave The Labs better than they found it.
hero.status: First pins: our two steering committees
hero.pinAlt: The Contributing Member pin, turning to follow your pointer

idea.title: Some people use the playbook. Some people write the next page.
idea.lede: This pin is for the second kind: people whose work The Labs now runs on. A playbook, a kit, a process, a first program. There's no application and no checklist. It's given by the people who saw the work.

items.label: Given
items.title: Never sold.
items.body: Dues get you a Supporting Member button, and our thanks. The pin only comes from work.

items.label: Recorded
items.title: One line, for good.
items.body: The register keeps your name, your number and a sentence on what you did.

items.label: Pinned
items.title: In person.
items.body: Handed to you at a gathering, by people who know exactly what it's for.

first.title: Before there were ranks, there were people doing the work anyway.
first.body: Our two steering committees get the first Contributing Member pins. They built The Labs before there was anything to earn.

rings.title: Every ring is earned.
rings.lede: The pin says you contributed. The rings say how far you've carried it. Scroll, and watch it grow.

steps.line: You made something we now run on.
steps.body: Recognized for real work on The Labs itself. No formal requirement. It's given by people who saw it.

steps.line: You've done it, so you can judge it.
steps.body: A Practitioner in two roles, sponsored by two Reviewers. You review changes, and new Practitioners, in the roles you know.

steps.line: You've helped everywhere. Now you can say yes.
steps.body: You've helped in every core area of The Labs. You approve changes to your Lab's playbooks, within a written grant from the board.

steps.line: You set the standard others build to.
steps.body: You shape the standard for an area. The board keeps the final say.

rings.names: Rank names are drafts, borrowed from open-source projects, until the board decides. [PLACEHOLDER]

metal.title: The metal says where the work happened.
metal.lede: Brass for work in your region. Silver for work across the whole network. Same pin, same rings, different shine.
metal.stageLabel: The {rank} pin in {metal}. Drag, or use the arrow keys, to turn it.

finish.coverAlt: Low close-up of the brass rings, brushed in fine radiating lines, stepping down from the red enamel
finish.title: Light runs around it.
finish.lede: Each ring is brushed in fine lines that radiate from the center, the way a good watch dial is. Tilt it, and a sweep of light turns with you.

details.title: Cut bright at every step.
details.body: The edge of each ring is polished, so every step draws its own thin line of light.
details.alt: Low-angle close-up of the silver rings' polished, stepped edges

details.title: One piece, not a stack.
details.body: The rings are struck into the pin itself. Nothing rattles, nothing comes loose, and it sits flat on a jacket. Each rank is its own pin, so the old one is yours to keep.
details.alt: Close-up of the brass pin: the enamel orb and swoosh inside three stepped, brushed rings

given.title: It starts with the work. It ends with a handshake.

steps.title: Do the work.
steps.body: Make something The Labs can reuse, or practice the roles a rank asks for.

steps.title: Someone vouches.
steps.body: People who already hold the pin put your name forward. For a rank, that's two sponsors, from different roles or Labs.

steps.title: It's recorded.
steps.body: Your Lab checks it, and HQ writes it on the register with a line on what you did.

steps.title: Pinned.
steps.body: At the next regional gathering. Your sponsors pin it on and say a sentence about why.

given.note: Who confers the Contributing Member pin is still being decided. [PLACEHOLDER]

true.title: A few things that don't change.
items: No one can buy a pin, a ring or a vote.
A pin records what you did. It doesn't expire.
Recognition isn't certification. It's the community saying thank you.
Step back whenever you need to. You keep the pin and the title.

register.title: Recognized so far.
register.empty: No one yet. The first pins go to our two steering committees.
register.label: The register, {n} entries

join.title: Every pin starts with one contribution.
join.lede: The way in today is the ambassador program. Tell your story, bring someone to their first workshop, and see what you end up building.

footer.renders: Images of the pin are 3D renders, not photos. The finish is the design; the real pin is still being made.
